notes: kb/Work PB5188 landed. §1985:VI.5.14.3 SR5: "An index data item can be referenced explicitly only in a SEARCH or SET statement, a relation condition, the USING phrase of a Procedure Division header, or the USING phrase of a CALL statement." The operand positions ask OperandContextRules.IndexDataItemAdmittedAt, the one edition-aware reading of the operand-context table's SR10 column: below COBOL-2002 the intrinsic function argument row answers no (the 2002 list, §2002:13.16.58.2 SR9, adds it), and ExpressionBinder.OperandRef refuses the argument (COBOL6979), so FUNCTION ORD-MAX (IX IY), LENGTH (IX), MAX and MIN over index data items are refused at 85. The arithmetic, subscript, reference-modifier and PERFORM VARYING positions refuse it through their class screen (COBOL0844), Sr1ClassRefusal refuses it in MOVE and the implicit moves (COBOL0809), and two positions no edition's list names now refuse it at every edition: a SORT or MERGE key (SortKeyAdmission.Violation, COBOL1757) and a report SOURCE identifier-1 (ReportWriterBinder.ScreenSourceIdentifier asks §2023:14.9.25.3 SR1's sending half, COBOL2770); the CONTROL clause is COBOL1700. Accepted at 85: SET, SEARCH VARYING, a relation condition and CALL USING. Witnesses: pb5188_index_data_item_function_argument_refused_at_85, pb5188-sort-merge-key-index-data-item, pb5188-source-index-data-item.

next.reason: 1985: "only in a SEARCH or SET statement, a relation condition, the USING phrase of a Procedure Division header, or the USING phrase of a CALL"; 2023: "an intrinsic function argument, an inline method invocation argument, ... or the USING phrase of a CALL or INVOKE statement". 2023 also allows an index data item as an intrinsic function argument, which the 1985 rule forbids; inline method invocation and INVOKE are new contexts.
